subject: Re: Renewal pricing: elastic commit paths & uplift cap options
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@brightbridge.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBridge AI Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options: commit tiers and uplift caps

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you are well — our renewal is coming up in July and usage has materially increased since we signed our current commit. We need to understand what flexible commit/discount options Redwood can offer that: (1) let us keep predictable unit pricing for planning, (2) avoid ballooning invoices if we spike, and (3) give us a path to larger committed discounts without a large immediate financial burden.

Specifically:
- Can you outline per-token discount tiers for hosted API usage? We currently sit at ~5B tokens/month and expect 25–40% growth.
- Is there an uplift cap (e.g., maximum allowed increase to committed volume at renewal vs. prior year) you enforce?
- Do you support phased increases (quarterly true-ups) rather than a single-year commit?

We can share recent usage exports if that helps. Ideally we want options that preserve our unit economics but don't lock us into over-commit during an uncertain growth period.

Thanks — copying procurement for timing.

Best,
Alex Chen
VP of Platform
BrightBridge AI

Attachment: BrightBridge_usage_Q1-Q2.csv (text/csv, 42KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit tiers and uplift caps

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear context and the heads-up on timing. This is an important ask and we have a couple of established paths that map to the trade-offs you called out. I've attached a short options packet with examples (RBW-commit-options-20270512.pdf). High level:

Option A — Conservative commit + per-token slabs:
- Year 1 commit anchored to current 3-month trailing average (you mentioned ~5B/month).
- Per-token discounts in slabs (0–2B @ baseline rate, 2–6B @ -8%, 6B+ @ -15%) — example only, we can rebalance thresholds.
- Quarterly soft true-ups: you reconcile usage vs. commit quarterly; overage billed at a modest uplift instead of list price.

Option B — Phased elastic increases (recommended for high-uncertainty scalers):
- Start Year 1 at a conservative commit (e.g., current baseline).
- Option to increase commit at quarterly checkpoints up to a pre-agreed ceiling (we typically cap uplift at 25–35% YoY for pricing sanity).
- When you opt-in to increase a quarter, the marginal buckets (per-token discount) apply prospectively.

Option C — Larger commit with ramp credits:
- Larger upfront commit for deeper unit discounts; we provide ramp credits to offset the first-month spike risk.

A couple notes: we can put hard ceilings on per-token price (per-token ceiling) so you never pay more than X for host inference regardless of slab mismatches. Also, we can include a short true-up window for seasonal customers (quarterly or a single true-up at 60 days) depending on your finance preference.

If youre open, I suggest a 30-minute call this week so Rishi (pricing) and I can walk through with your procurement team and run a modeled P&L for each path.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

Attachment: RBW-commit-options-20270512.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Renewal options: commit tiers and uplift caps — internal pricing note

Kimberly / Marcus — internal note on acceptable guardrails for this account: BrightBridge is mid-enterprise but high growth. Recommended approach to present:

- Default uplift cap: 30% YoY on committed volume without requiring executive repricing. Anything >30% should route to sales leadership for approval.
- Phased increases: allow quarterly opt-ins up to the uplift cap. Each opt-in triggers the marginal slab pricing prospectively.
- Per-token ceiling: offer a ceiling equal to list price minus 5% so procurement has predictability in worst-case.
- True-up cadence: quarterly soft true-ups with one true-up grace (i.e., first overage within 60 days can be credited back if usage stabilizes).

Margin impact: this preserves predictable economics and keeps downside limited. If Kimberly wants, we can include a short-term ramp credit (1–2 months) for initial spikes.

Rishi
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics

From: Alex Chen <alex@brightbridge.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBridge AI Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit tiers and uplift caps

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement:

1) The procurement lead wants a firm maximum uplift cap in writing (we prefer a number rather than "typical"). Is 30% a hard limit or negotiable?
2) If we do phased increases, will the new commit increments require a 12‑month minimum at the increased level or can they be ratcheted quarterly?
3) We'd prefer quarterly true-ups, but is there a single end-of-year true-up option (to reconcile seasonality across quarters) we can choose instead?

I've attached our usage export for the last two quarters so you can model slabs against real data.

Appreciate the clarity — we want a model that our finance team can forecast.

Alex

Attachment: BrightBridge_usage_Q1-Q2.csv (text/csv, 42KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@brightbridge.ai>, BrightBridge AI Procurement <procurement@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit tiers and uplift caps — proposal

Alex / procurement team — thanks for the data and the specific Qs. Based on your Q1–Q2 cadence and forecasted growth, here is a clean proposal (summary attached and pasted below). We kept the language deliberately prescriptive so procurement can circulate.

Summary proposal (illustrative numbers linked to your usage file):
- Year 1 commit: 5B tokens/month baseline (anchored to trailing average).
- Pricing slabs (per-token discounts off list): 0–2B @ 0% (list), 2–6B @ 9% discount, 6B+ @ 17% discount.
- Phased increase path: quarterly opt-in to increase commit in +5% increments up to a hard uplift cap of 30% YoY.
- Commitment ratchet: any opt-in that increases the committed baseline becomes the new baseline for the next quarter; no 12-month hold required beyond the renewal cycle (we anchor annual contracts at renewal).
- True-up: quarterly soft true-up with an annual reconciliation option at renewal (your choice). Overages during a quarter billed at the per-token ceiling rate (list minus 5%); if annual reconciliation shows total commit > billed, we will credit back the difference.
- Ramp credit: two-month 50% credit on incremental usage above the committed baseline in the first quarter post-renewal to ease transition.

Next steps: if this aligns, I'll prepare a short commercial term sheet and route for legal review. Ive attached the term sheet PDF for redlines.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kimberly_proposal_20270518.pdf (application/pdf, 85KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@brightbridge.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options: commit tiers and uplift caps — approval to proceed

Alex / team — I reviewed Kimberlys proposal and Rishis guardrails. The uplift cap at 30% and the quarterly opt-in path look reasonable for BrightBridges profile.

Kimberly: please proceed to a commercial term sheet and include the HubSpot deal link for exec sign-off. Rishi: can you lock the per-token ceiling and ramp credit mechanics into the commercial language so procurement has exact pricing callouts?

Happy to jump on a 15-minute call if final approval needs a quick exec alignment.

Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, US
